question.problem:
Given that the random variables 

$$
X_1\sim N(-1,2^2), \qquad
X_2\sim  N(3, 3^2), \qquad 
X_3\sim N(4,2)
$$

are mutually independent, what is the distribution of $Y = X_1 + X_2 + X_3?$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X_1, X_2,$ and $X_3$ are mutually independent random variables, where 

$$
X_1\sim N(\mu_1,\sigma^2_1),\qquad 
X_2\sim N(\mu_2,\sigma^2_2),\qquad
X_3\sim N(\mu_3,\sigma^2_3),
$$

then 

$$
\begin{aligned}Y & ={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3} \\  & ∼N({\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2}+{\mu }_{3},\,{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+{\sigma }_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have

$$
X_1\sim N(-1,2^2), \qquad
X_2\sim  N(3, 3^2), \qquad 
X_3\sim N(4,2),
$$

and

$$
Y = X_1 + X_2 + X_3.
$$

Since $X_1, X_2,$ and $X_3$ are mutually independent, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\mu }_{1}+{\mu }_{2}+{\mu }_{3} \\  & =-1+3+4 \\  & =6, \\ \text{Var}[Y] & ={\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+{\sigma }_{3}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+2 \\  & =4+9+2 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}+{X}_{2}+{X}_{3} & ∼N(6,15).\end{aligned}
$$
